record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: For the bi-grading ray (N, 2N), beginning at which N′>7 do nontrivial cocycles ω in the graph-complex kernel ker d exist, and beginning at which larger N′′ are those cocycles orientable to nonzero Kontsevich graphs built from wedges? Can one give explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P) using known cocycles γ and new cocycles ω on that ray?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Starting which N′ > 7, are there nontrivial cocycles ω ∈ ker d ? And starting which N′′ > N′, are these cocycles orientable (i.e. meeting no obstructions [9, App. A]) to nonzero Kontsevich’s graphs built from wedges ← •→? Give explicit examples of new symmetries P˙ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m≠0 · O→r(γ)(P) for known cocycles γ and new such ω on the ray (N, 2N).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Kontsevich's graph complex of finite undirected graphs on N vertices and 2N edges (for N ≥ 1), graded by the number of vertices and edges, equipped with the vertex-expansion differential d. A cocycle ω is an element of ker d. Along the bi-grading ray (#V, #E) = (N, 2N), the well-known wheel cocycles γ_{2ℓ+1} (the tetrahedron γ_3 at N=4, the pentagon-wheel γ_5 at N=6, the heptagon-wheel γ_7 at N=8, ...) are known to exist. For an undirected graph cocycle ω, let O→r(ω)(P) denote Kontsevich's orientation morphism producing, when no obstructions occur, an oriented graph cocycle built from wedges ←•→ which encodes an infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ = O→r(ω)(P) of any Poisson structure P on an affine manifold.

Solve the following:
(a) Determine the smallest integer N′ > 7 such that there exists a nontrivial cocycle ω ∈ ker d in the graph complex on the ray (N′, 2N′) that is not in the linear span of the previously known wheel cocycles.
(b) Determine the smallest integer N″ ≥ N′ such that some such new cocycle ω on the ray (N″, 2N″) is orientable, i.e. encounters no obstruction in passing through O→r(·) to a nonzero oriented Kontsevich graph cocycle built from wedges.
(c) Provide explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form
   Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P),  m ≠ 0,
where γ is a known wheel cocycle and ω is a new cocycle constructed in part (b).
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources confirm that on the ray (N, 2N) the known wheel cocycles γ_3, γ_5, γ_7 exist at N = 4, 6, 8, but no published computation appears to identify a new nontrivial cocycle at N′ > 7 nor establish its orientability or produce explicit composite Poisson-bracket symmetries of the stated form. The problem is presented as an explicit open problem in the relevant literature with no resolution found.

status_evidence.title: The heptagon-wheel cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex
status_evidence.snippet: The heptagon-wheel cocycle at ℓ=3 consists of 46 graphs on 8 vertices and 14 edges.
status_evidence.claim: Known wheel cocycles populate the ray (N,2N) up through N=8.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems concerning new cocycles on the ray (N,2N) and their orientability.
status_evidence.claim: The existence and orientability of new cocycles for N>7 is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Poisson brackets symmetry from the pentagon-wheel cocycle in the graph complex
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs Poisson bracket symmetries from known wheel cocycles via the orientation morphism.
status_evidence.claim: Symmetries of the form Ṗ = O→r(γ)(P) are explicitly known only for known wheel cocycles γ.
